named_other_account_result.applied_fact: For incomparable a,b with Pred(b) subseteq Pred(a), p_ab=1-(Q+R)/(2E), 2I=Q-R, and reverse nonneutral blockers are lower blockers of a or upper blockers of b. The new funnel theorem proves the inclusion hypothesis for every first-boundary sibling pair and uses the exact R structure to force continuation in the strict branch.

secondary_other_account_result.applied_fact: Every incomparable pair with exactly one relation-distinguisher is balanced; hence a hypothetical counterexample sibling pair has at least two distinguishers.

essential_steps: At the inherited first-boundary two-cover Hasse fork x<.s1,x<.s2, every lower distinguisher lies after B2. Width at most three forces Pred(s1),Pred(s2) to be nested, and the proper difference to be a chain; opposite-side predecessor differences would make {x,y,d,e} a four-antichain.

In the strict branch Pred(b) proper-subset Pred(a), the unique top d of the predecessor-difference chain is a Hasse predecessor d<.a, giving an incoming Hasse bow-tie d<.a>.x<.b with {x,y,d} a three-antichain.

If the larger-predecessor sibling a is majority-early (a prec_* b), then Q+R<2E/3. No span descent forces exactly two minimal successor blockers of a relative to b, both Hasse successors. If the larger-predecessor sibling is majority-late (b prec_* a), then either (b,d) is a shorter extreme pair or the exact reverse-remainder identity forces a minimal Hasse successor blocker of b relative to a; without span descent it lies after a.

exhaustive_refinement: If the predecessor difference is empty, there are at least two successor distinguishers and the prior equal-predecessor channel theorem applies. If its chain has size one, at least one successor distinguisher is also forced. If there is no successor distinguisher, the delayed predecessor-difference chain has size at least two.
